problem: Given that the expression $2\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ can be written as $R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-ϕ)$ with ${0}^{∘}<ϕ<{90}^{∘}$ and $R>0$, what is the value of $ϕ?$

activity_context.topic_title: Writing Sums of Trigonometric Functions in Amplitude-Phase Form

feedback.worked_solution:
The sum formula for sine gives

$$
\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x+ϕ) & =R(\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ+\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) \\  & =R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by writing the given expression in the amplitude-phase form

$$
\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+3\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x+ϕ),
$$

we get the following identity:

$$
\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+3\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)=(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)
$$

Equating the coefficients of $\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)$ and $\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x),$ we get the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ=\sqrt{3} \\ R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ=3\end{aligned}
$$

Dividing the second equation by the first, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}{R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ} & =\frac{3}{\sqrt{3}} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡ϕ & =\sqrt{3} \\ ϕ & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\sqrt{3}) \\  & ={60}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the amplitude $R.$ Squaring the first and the second equations of the system and adding the results together, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)}^{2}+{(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)}^{2} & =(\sqrt{3})^{2}+{3}^{2} \\ {R}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡ϕ+{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ) & =3+9 \\ {R}^{2} & =12 \\ R & =2\sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we only consider the positive root since $R>0.$

Finally, we can write the initial expression in amplitude-phase form as follows:

$$
\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+3\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)=2\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x+{60}^{∘})
$$
